answer.summary: Invoice SFS-55120 for $9,870 shows the classic signs of a vendor-impersonation (business email compromise) attempt. It came from accounts@summitfaci1ity.example, a lookalike domain that swaps one letter for the digit '1'. The supplier's registered remit email is accounts@summitfacility.example. On 2026-10-13, two days before the invoice arrived, a request from that same lookalike address changed the supplier's bank account from ending 5927 to ending 6122, and no call-back was done. The invoice now asks for payment to the 6122 account in 7 days, although the agreed terms are NET30, and the amount is about 2.6 times the supplier's median invoice of $3,752.81 (the 90th percentile is $4,083.10).

evidence.text: Registered remit email is accounts@summitfacility.example; terms NET30; median invoice $3,752.81, p90 $4,083.10 over 18 invoices; bank on file now ends 6122.
Bank account changed 2026-10-13 from last4 5927 to 6122 by E30655, requested by email from accounts@summitfaci1ity.example, callback_verified false.
